phases.message: I'm Rosa, I run freight claims at Thistlewood Lighting. Start in Tracklog: read every shipment with an exception, and open each one for its carrier, its bill of lading terms and its delivery receipt.
Mailnest has the claims folder: our customers' damage reports and the carriers' letters. Read every message, and note when and how each damage or shortage was found.
Docshelf has our claims checklist, the invoices, our packing records and the inspection reports. Read what each claim would rest on.

Harrowgate Freight's claims portal. Read its claim rules and the claims we already have open, then file every claim Harrowgate owes us, for the amount it owes, with the proof. Don't file anything it doesn't owe.

Larkfield LTL's claims centre. Read its rules and what we already have open with Larkfield, and file what Larkfield owes us. Then tell me what you filed, what is due next, and what you left alone and why.

documents.title: Thistlewood's freight claims checklist
documents.text: Today is Friday 9 October 2026. Our checklist, from 49 CFR Part 370 and our carriers' terms. 1. A claim is a written claim to the carrier that moved the freight (the one that picked it up or delivered it), identifying the shipment, asserting the carrier's liability and asking for a specified amount. A notation on a delivery receipt, an inspection report or a trace request is not a claim. 2. Amount: our actual loss, the invoice price to our customer of each unit lost or broken (invoices in Docshelf). Freight is prepaid and not claimed; broken units have no salvage value. 3. On a released-value shipment, claim the released value (the article's weight times the rate per pound) when it is less than the loss. 4. Attach the bill of lading, the delivery receipt, the invoice and, for damage, the photos and any inspection report. 5. File within the carrier's time limit (never less than 9 months, by federal law). 6. We do not claim damage that happened after delivery, or damage our own packing caused.

harrowgate_rules.text: Today is Friday 9 October 2026. Harrowgate Freight's cargo claim rules for shippers, from 49 U.S.C. 14706 (the Carmack Amendment), 49 CFR Part 370 and Harrowgate's own Rules Tariff HGF-100. Topics: liability, filing, time-limits, concealed, released-value, defences, handling.

49 U.S.C. 14706(a): the receiving carrier and the delivering carrier are liable for the actual loss or injury to the property they carry. Harrowgate answers for freight it picked up or delivered. It does not answer for freight another carrier picked up and delivered alone: claim that against that carrier.

49 CFR 370.3(b): a claim is a written communication that identifies the shipment, asserts Harrowgate's liability for the loss or damage, and claims a specified or determinable amount. 370.3(c): a notation of shortage or damage on a delivery receipt, a bad order report or an inspection report does not, standing alone, make a claim. 370.7(b): attach the bill of lading, the invoice, and proof of the loss. One claim per bill of lading.

Harrowgate's bill of lading terms: a claim must be filed within 9 months after delivery, or, for a shipment not delivered, within 9 months after the bill of lading date. A carrier may not allow less than 9 months (49 U.S.C. 14706(e)(1)). A claim filed after that is declined. Suit must be brought within 2 years from the date Harrowgate gives written notice that it disallows any part of a claim.

Rules Tariff HGF-100, item 410: concealed loss or damage (found after a delivery receipt was signed without exception) should be reported to Harrowgate within 5 business days of delivery, with the cartons and packing kept for inspection. A clean delivery receipt is evidence of good-order delivery, not a bar to a claim; the claimant shows the goods were tendered in good order and the damage happened before delivery. Item 410 does not shorten the 9 months to file a claim.

Rules Tariff HGF-100, item 780, under 49 U.S.C. 14706(c)(1)(A): when the shipper chooses Harrowgate's released rate and signs the released-value declaration on the bill of lading, Harrowgate's liability for loss or damage is limited to $2.00 per pound of each lost or damaged article. On a released-value shipment, the claim is for the released value (the article's weight times $2.00) when that is less than the actual loss. Without a signed declaration, liability is the full actual loss.

As the Supreme Court held in Missouri Pacific R. Co. v. Elmore & Stahl, 377 U.S. 134 (1964), once the shipper shows good-order tender, damaged arrival and the amount, the carrier is liable unless it shows it was free from negligence and the damage came from an act of God, the public enemy, the act of the shipper itself (such as inadequate packing), public authority, or the inherent vice or nature of the goods. Harrowgate is not liable for damage after delivery.

49 CFR 370.5 and 370.9: Harrowgate acknowledges a claim in writing within 30 days of receiving it, and pays, declines or makes a firm compromise offer in writing within 120 days; if it cannot, it writes to the claimant then and every 60 days with the claim's status and the reason for the delay. Do not file a second claim for a bill of lading already claimed.

larkfield_rules.text: Today is Friday 9 October 2026. Larkfield LTL's claim rules, from 49 U.S.C. 14706, 49 CFR Part 370, Larkfield's bill of lading terms and its Rules Tariff LKF-500. Topics: liability, filing, time-limits, tracing, defences, handling.

Under 49 U.S.C. 14706(a), Larkfield is liable for the actual loss of or injury to property it picks up or delivers. Larkfield has no released-value rates: every Larkfield shipment moves at full value. Larkfield is not liable for freight another carrier moved alone.

Submit a claim in writing in the claims centre: it must identify the shipment, assert Larkfield's liability and claim a specified amount (49 CFR 370.3(b)). Attach the bill of lading, the delivery receipt, the invoice, and for a lost shipment the consignee's statement that it was not received from any other source (370.7(c)). One claim per bill of lading.

Larkfield's bill of lading terms: a claim for damage or shortage must be submitted within 9 months after delivery; a claim for a shipment never delivered within 9 months after the bill of lading date. Federal law forbids a shorter period (49 U.S.C. 14706(e)(1)). Suit within 2 years of Larkfield's written disallowance.
A trace request asks Larkfield to find freight. It is not a claim (49 CFR 370.3(c)), and it does not stop the time to file a claim from running.

Larkfield is not liable for loss or damage caused by an act of God, the public enemy, the shipper's own act, public authority or the goods' inherent vice, if it was itself free from negligence; nor for damage after delivery, once the consignee has taken the freight.

Larkfield acknowledges a claim within 30 days of receiving it, and pays, declines or makes a firm compromise offer in writing within 120 days, with a written status every 60 days after that while it is pending (49 CFR 370.5, 370.9). A claim already submitted is not submitted again.
